title: UP-DETR: Unsupervised Pre-training for Object Detection with Transformers

problem.summary: DETR trains its transformer encoder-decoder from scratch, needing large-scale data and extremely long schedules even on COCO, and performing poorly when data is scarce (e.g. PASCAL VOC); existing unsupervised pretext tasks target CNN backbones and cannot pre-train DETR's transformer.
statements: Trained with scratch transformers, DETR needs large-scale training data and an extreme long training schedule even on COCO.
DETR performs poorly on PASCAL VOC, which has insufficient training data and fewer instances than COCO.
Existing contrastive pretext tasks focus on feature discrimination rather than the spatial localization the DETR transformer performs.
Popular unsupervised methods pre-train the backbone, but DETR's transformer (about 18.0M parameters) has never been pre-trained.

evidence.quote: However, trained with scratch transformers, DETR needs large-scale training data and an extreme long training schedule even on COCO dataset.
Besides, it is found that DETR performs poorly in PASCAL VOC dataset [6] which has insufficient training data and fewer instances than COCO.
existing pretext tasks can not directly apply to pre-train the transformer in DETR.

background.summary: The work builds on DETR (set prediction with a Transformer encoder-decoder and Hungarian matching), self-supervised/unsupervised pre-training (MoCo, SwAV, SimCLR, BERT-style language model pre-training), and vision transformers. The gap claimed is that no existing pretext task trains the spatial-localization behaviour of DETR's transformer.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.relation: base architecture whose transformer is pre-trained
relatedWork.quote: DETR [1] is a recent object detection framework that is conceptually simpler without hand-crafted process by direct set prediction [25], which assigns the positive and negative samples automatically.

relatedWork.name: Masked language model (BERT)
relatedWork.relation: prior transformer pre-training paradigm from NLP
relatedWork.quote: For natural language processing, utilizing time sequence relationship between discrete tokens, masked language model [9], permutation language model [29] and auto regressive model [7], [8] are proposed to pre-train transformers [2] for language representation.

relatedWork.name: MoCo / SwAV
relatedWork.relation: prior unsupervised visual representation learning used for the frozen CNN
relatedWork.quote: For computer vision, unsupervised pre-training models also achieve remarkable progress recently for visual representation learning, outperforming the supervised learning counterpart in downstream tasks.

relatedWork.name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
relatedWork.relation: contemporaneous transformer backbone design contrasted with DETR
relatedWork.quote: The pioneering work is Vision Transformer (ViT) [33], which applies a transformer on non-overlapping image patches for image classification.

evidence.quote: we need to construct a spatial localization related task to pre-train the transformer in DETR.
Therefore, existing pre-training tasks of backbones [10], [11], [37] can not be simply applied to DETR.

solution.summary: UP-DETR pre-trains the DETR transformer with a random query patch detection pretext task: patches are randomly cropped from an unlabeled image, added to object queries, and the decoder must localize them; a frozen SwAV CNN backbone, patch feature reconstruction loss, multi-query patch assignment and an attention mask handle the multi-task and multi-query issues, after which the model is fine-tuned for object or one-shot detection.
solution.approach: Turn pre-training into an unsupervised set-prediction problem in which randomly cropped query patches are found in the image by the transformer decoder without any human annotations.
components: random query patch detection pretext task on ImageNet without labels
frozen SwAV-pre-trained CNN backbone during transformer pre-training
patch feature reconstruction loss Lrec (MSE between l2-normalized features)
multi-query patch detection: N=100 object queries split into M=10 patch groups
attention mask matrix added to decoder self-attention softmax
Hungarian matching with class-balance weight lambda (M/N for negatives)
fine-tuning with unchanged DETR architecture for object detection or one-shot detection

evidence.quote: we propose a novel pretext task named random query patch detection in Unsupervised Pre-training DETR (UP-DETR).
we randomly crop multiple query patches from the given image, and pre-train the transformer for object detection to predict the bounding boxes of these query patches in the given image.
We argue that the frozen pre-training backbone is the most essential step to the success of UP-DETR.
we utilize an attention mask matrix to control the interactions between different object queries.

experiments.summary: The transformer is pre-trained on the unlabeled 1.28M ImageNet training set (60 epochs, eight V100 GPUs) and fine-tuned on PASCAL VOC and COCO, comparing against DETR and Faster R-CNN under matched settings; transfer is also evaluated on one-shot detection and panoptic segmentation, with ablations on query-patch count, frozen CNN, feature reconstruction and the attention mask.

evidence.quote: In our experiments, UP-DETR significantly boosts the performance of DETR with faster convergence and higher average precision on object detection, one-shot detection and panoptic segmentation.
UP-DETR obtains 43.1 AP on COCO, which is 1.0 AP better than DETR (SwAV CNN) and 1.1 AP better than Faster R-CNN (R50-FPN) (9× schedule).

limitations.summary: UP-DETR still trails Faster R-CNN on small objects because it lacks an FPN-like neck, it depends on an already pre-trained SwAV CNN, a gap between patch-level ImageNet pre-training and multi-object detection fine-tuning remains, and the attention mask gives no noticeable downstream gain.
items: Small-object AP lags Faster R-CNN because of the lacking of FPN-like architecture.
The method heavily relies on an externally pre-trained CNN (SwAV) since the CNN is frozen during transformer pre-training.
The gap between patch-level pre-training on ImageNet and labeled fine-tuning on COCO/VOC cannot be eliminated.
After downstream fine-tuning there is no noticeable difference between models pre-trained with and without the attention mask.

evidence.quote: Regrettably, UP-DETR is still slightly lagging behind Faster R-CNN in APS , because of the lacking of FPN-like architecture [43].
It is worth noting that UP-DETR with frozen CNN and feature reconstruction heavily relies on a pre-trained CNN model, e.g. SwAV CNN.
However, the gap between pre-training and fine-tuning always exists.

futureDirections.direction: Combine random query patch detection with contrastive learning to pre-train the whole DETR model from scratch.
futureDirections.quote: Therefore, we believe that it is a promising direction to further investigate UP-DETR with random query patch detection and contrastive learning together to pre-train the whole DETR model from scratch.

futureDirections.direction: Integrate CNN and transformer pre-training into one end-to-end framework and extend UP-DETR to few-shot detection and object tracking.
futureDirections.quote: We hope an advanced method can integrate the CNN and transformer pretraining into a unified end-to-end framework and apply UP-DETR to more downstream tasks (e.g. few-shot object detection and object tracking).

equations.name: Pre-training Hungarian loss
equations.expr: L(y, y_hat) = sum_i [ lambda_{c_i} L_cls(c_i, c_hat_{sigma(i)}) + 1{c_i=1} L_box(b_i, b_hat) + 1{c_i=1} L_rec(p_i, p_hat) ]

equations.name: Attention mask
equations.expr: X_{i,j} = 0 if i,j in the same group, -inf otherwise

deploymentClaims: UP-DETR has exactly the same FLOPs, parameters and running FPS as the authors' DETR re-implementation
Pre-training runs 60 epochs with batch size 256 on eight Nvidia V100 GPUs
Code and pre-training models released at github.com/dddzg/up-detr

evidence.quote: So, they have exactly the same FLOPs, parameters and running FPS.
UP-DETR converges much faster with a higher AP than DETR.
